note: Exporter versions are pinned here (models.md 6.5). `tag` values are null until the owner pins them; a real export refuses a null tag. The command templates are the implementer's reading of each tool's command line and are UNVERIFIED against the pinned versions: check them with the first real export. Placeholders: {merged} {out_dir} {variant} {outfile} {bf16_gguf} {script} {quantize_bin}. QWEN3.5 EXPORTS ARE UNVERIFIED (2026-11-16): the models are a hybrid architecture (Gated DeltaNet plus attention) published as multimodal `...ForConditionalGeneration` checkpoints. The converter commands below were written for plain transformer models; whether they export a merged fine-tune of the hybrid architecture is THE FIRST THING TO TEST on the Windows PC (models.md 9.1 step 9), with the untrained candidate, before any training. Browser: transformers.js 4.0.0 or later supports `qwen3_5_text`, and onnx-community/Qwen3.5-0.8B-Text-ONNX shows a text-only q4f16 build of about 0.5 GB running on WebGPU; the export must be text-only (no vision tower), so `text_only` is true. Pin `transformers_js.tag` to a 4.x tag. GGUF: llama.cpp supports the architectures (pin a tag recent enough); a fine-tuned Qwen3.5 may fail to convert with "BPE pre-tokenizer not recognized" (models.md 10).
first_test_on_pc: merge a LoRA on the untrained candidate and save it
convert the merged folder to GGUF with convert_hf_to_gguf.py
convert the merged folder to text-only ONNX q4f16 with the transformers.js script
run the template check (Python, transformers.js, llama.cpp) on the golden cases
